findings.antecedent: order of the experimental conditions (windowless condition first)
findings.consequent: window effect on eye symptoms (window vs. windowless)
findings.mechanism: each participants' experience in the first session may have influenced the result of eye symptoms... in the second session.
findings.quote: In comparing the window to the windowless condition (Z = -2.85, p = 0.004, r = 0.31), the participants who had the windowless condition first reported experiencing much fewer eye symptoms in the window condition (Mdifference = 0.40) than the participants who had the window condition first (Mdifference = 0.03).

findings.antecedent: order of the experimental conditions (windowless condition first)
findings.consequent: window effect on perceived stress level (window vs. windowless)
findings.mechanism: each participants' experience in the first session may have influenced the result of... perceived stress level in the second session.
findings.quote: Similarly, in comparing the window to windowless condition (Z = -2.76, p = 0.006, r = 0.30), the participants who had the windowless condition first reported experiencing a higher perceived level of stress in the window condition (Mdifference = 0.33) compared to the participants who had the window condition first (M = 0.11).

stimuli.description: office-like test room with and without windows, providing a view of shaded trees and sunny sky, with controlled air and window surface temperature (28 °C)

tables.description: Potential factors that may moderate the effect of the experimental conditions (with or without windows) on the outcome measures.
Z-statistics, statistical significance (p-value; permutation test), and effect size (r) for the effect of being in the space with windows versus without on emotion.

limitations: Potential contribution of non-visual effects from daylight on the outcome variables (confounding of daylight and view).
Assessed the effect of a window view only in a slightly warm condition (28 °C).
Findings are based on a specific natural view (mostly trees, sunny sky) from the chamber windows, limiting generalizability to different view contents or qualities.
Tested a very short-term exposure (55 min) to the different window conditions.
Effect sizes were small (ranging from 0.29 to 0.36) based on Ferguson's thresholds.
